text: A study analyzed the stem cell marker Nanog gene for lung cancer diagnosis and prognosis. 100 patients diagnosed between April 2013 and May 2015 were randomly divided into group A (lung cancer) and group B (squamous cell lung carcinoma). RT-PCR detected Nanog expression in cancer and adjacent tissues. No significant intergroup difference existed in age, gender, disease stage, or lymph node metastasis. Nanog expression was significantly higher in carcinoma than adjacent tissues (p<0.05). Differentiated and well-differentiated carcinoma showed significantly higher Nanog expression than poorly differentiated and undifferentiated carcinoma (p<0.05). Nanog was highly expressed in CD44+ cells and significantly higher in lung cancer stem cells (p<0.05). Stage III and IV patients had higher Nanog expression, and lower cell differentiation was associated with strong Nanog expression.
